nodes.author: supabase

nodes.label: SECURITY DEFINER Functions Bypass RLS
nodes.author: supabase
nodes.rationale: Never add SECURITY DEFINER to fix a permission error; functions in public are callable by anon/authenticated by default. Prefer SECURITY INVOKER.

nodes.label: UPDATE Policies Require USING and WITH CHECK
nodes.author: supabase
nodes.norm_label: update policies require using and with check
nodes.rationale: Without WITH CHECK a user can reassign user_id; UPDATE also needs a SELECT policy or silently affects 0 rows.

nodes.label: Never Use user_metadata in JWT Authorization
nodes.author: supabase
nodes.norm_label: never use user_metadata in jwt authorization
nodes.rationale: raw_user_meta_data is user-editable; store authorization data in app_metadata.

nodes.label: Batch INSERT Statements for Bulk Data
nodes.norm_label: batch insert statements for bulk data
nodes.rationale: Individual inserts each cost a round trip and transaction; batching ~1000 rows per statement or using COPY is 10-50x faster. Impact: MEDIUM.

nodes.label: Eliminate N+1 Queries with Batch Loading
nodes.norm_label: eliminate n+1 queries with batch loading
nodes.rationale: Querying once per item in a loop causes N+1 round trips; batch with ANY(array) or a JOIN for a single round trip. Impact: MEDIUM-HIGH.

nodes.label: Consistent lock ordering (SELECT ... ORDER BY id FOR UPDATE)
nodes.norm_label: consistent lock ordering (select ... order by id for update)

nodes.label: Prevent Deadlocks with Consistent Lock Ordering
nodes.norm_label: prevent deadlocks with consistent lock ordering
nodes.rationale: Deadlocks occur when transactions lock resources in different orders; acquire locks in consistent (e.g. ID) order or update in a single statement. Impact: MEDIUM-HIGH.

nodes.label: Keep Transactions Short to Reduce Lock Contention
nodes.norm_label: keep transactions short to reduce lock contention
nodes.rationale: Long transactions (e.g. holding locks across HTTP payment calls) block other queries; do external calls outside the transaction. Impact: MEDIUM-HIGH.

nodes.label: Choose Appropriate Data Types
nodes.rationale: Right types cut storage and prevent bugs: bigint ids, text over varchar(n), timestamptz, boolean, numeric for money. Impact: HIGH.

nodes.label: PendingPurchase Manual Approval

nodes.label: Autovacuum scale factor tuning
nodes.rationale: Lower vacuum/analyze scale factors (5%/2%) for high-churn tables.

nodes.label: Maintain Table Statistics with VACUUM and ANALYZE
nodes.norm_label: maintain table statistics with vacuum and analyze
nodes.rationale: Stale statistics make the planner choose poor plans; VACUUM reclaims space, ANALYZE refreshes stats. Impact: MEDIUM.

nodes.label: Random UUIDv4 Index Fragmentation
nodes.rationale: Random v4 UUIDs scatter inserts across the index and should be avoided as PKs on large tables.

nodes.label: Select Optimal Primary Key Strategy
nodes.rationale: PK choice affects insert performance, index size, and replication efficiency.

nodes.label: bigint GENERATED ALWAYS AS IDENTITY Primary Key
nodes.norm_label: bigint generated always as identity primary key
nodes.rationale: SQL-standard, sequential, 8 bytes; preferred over serial for single databases.

nodes.label: UUIDv7 / Time-Ordered Primary Key
nodes.rationale: Time-ordered IDs for distributed or exposed IDs avoid index fragmentation; requires pg_uuidv7 or time-prefixed text IDs.

nodes.label: Keyset (cursor) pagination
nodes.rationale: Cursor must include all sort columns, using row comparison like (created_at, id) > (...).

nodes.label: Use Cursor-Based Pagination Instead of OFFSET
nodes.norm_label: use cursor-based pagination instead of offset
nodes.rationale: OFFSET scans all skipped rows so deep pages get slower; keyset/cursor pagination uses the index and stays constant. Impact: MEDIUM-HIGH.

nodes.label: Use UPSERT for Insert-or-Update Operations
nodes.rationale: Select-then-insert has a race condition; INSERT ... ON CONFLICT is atomic. Impact: MEDIUM.

nodes.label: Leftmost prefix rule (equality columns first, range last)
nodes.norm_label: leftmost prefix rule (equality columns first, range last)

nodes.label: Create Composite Indexes for Multi-Column Queries
nodes.norm_label: create composite indexes for multi-column queries
nodes.rationale: One composite index beats combining separate single-column indexes via bitmap scan. Impact: HIGH.

nodes.label: Use Covering Indexes to Avoid Table Lookups
nodes.norm_label: use covering indexes to avoid table lookups
nodes.rationale: INCLUDE columns so queries can be served by index-only scans without heap fetches. Impact: MEDIUM-HIGH.

nodes.label: Use Partial Indexes for Filtered Queries
nodes.norm_label: use partial indexes for filtered queries
nodes.rationale: Indexing only rows matching a consistent WHERE condition (e.g. deleted_at is null) yields smaller, faster indexes. Impact: HIGH.

nodes.label: Use Lowercase Identifiers for Compatibility
nodes.rationale: PostgreSQL folds unquoted identifiers to lowercase; quoted mixed-case names require quotes forever and break tools, ORMs, and AI assistants.

nodes.label: Compatibility View for Mixed-Case Tables
nodes.rationale: If stuck with mixed-case identifiers, create snake_case views as a compatibility layer.

nodes.label: Partition Large Tables (Range by Time)
nodes.rationale: Partition tables over ~100M rows or time-series data so queries scan only relevant partitions and old data can be dropped instantly instead of slow DELETE/VACUUM.

nodes.label: Apply Principle of Least Privilege
nodes.rationale: Grant only minimum permissions and never use superuser for app queries so SQL injection is not catastrophic.

nodes.label: max_connections setting
nodes.rationale: Formula: (RAM MB / 5MB per connection) - reserved; recommended 100 for 4GB RAM.

nodes.label: work_mem setting
nodes.rationale: work_mem * max_connections should not exceed 25% of RAM.

nodes.label: Session pool mode
nodes.rationale: Connection held for whole session; needed for prepared statements and temp tables.

nodes.label: Transaction pool mode

nodes.label: Seq Scan / Rows Removed by Filter as missing-index signal
nodes.norm_label: seq scan / rows removed by filter as missing-index signal

nodes.label: Set Appropriate Connection Limits
nodes.rationale: Each connection uses 1-3MB RAM; excessive max_connections exhausts memory. Practically 100-200 connections beats the theoretical max for query performance. Impact: CRITICAL.

nodes.label: Use Connection Pooling for All Applications
nodes.norm_label: use connection pooling for all applications
nodes.rationale: Postgres connections are expensive; pooling lets 500 concurrent users share ~10 real connections. Impact: CRITICAL.

nodes.label: Use Prepared Statements Correctly with Pooling
nodes.norm_label: use prepared statements correctly with pooling
nodes.rationale: Prepared statements are bound to a single connection; in transaction-mode pooling the next request may get a different connection, causing 'prepared statement does not exist' errors. Impact: HIGH.

nodes.label: Use EXPLAIN ANALYZE to Diagnose Slow Queries
nodes.norm_label: use explain analyze to diagnose slow queries
nodes.rationale: Executing the query with actual timings reveals real bottlenecks instead of guessing. Impact: LOW-MEDIUM.

nodes.label: Enable pg_stat_statements for Query Analysis
nodes.rationale: Tracks execution statistics to identify slowest and most frequent queries. Impact: LOW-MEDIUM.

nodes.label: Add Indexes on WHERE and JOIN Columns
nodes.norm_label: add indexes on where and join columns
nodes.rationale: Unindexed filter/join columns cause full table scans that worsen as tables grow. Impact: CRITICAL.

nodes.label: Add Constraints Safely in Migrations
nodes.rationale: PostgreSQL lacks ADD CONSTRAINT IF NOT EXISTS; use a DO block checking pg_constraint for idempotent migrations. Impact: HIGH.

nodes.label: Index Foreign Key Columns
nodes.rationale: Postgres does not auto-index FK columns; missing indexes slow JOINs and ON DELETE CASCADE. Impact: HIGH.
